thread:
alex: Heads-up, getting a weird huge kernel blob in nsys right at our KV warmup. timeline shows ~250-350ms spike pre-steady-state, feels too big for the codepath.

alex: Here's the CLI I used:

alex: ```
nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt --output=kv-warmup-clip --duration=5000 --sample=cpu --capture-range=process:inference_sv
```

julia: Two quick suspects: 1) sampling artifacts from too-short duration, 2) missing NVTX brackets so the UI groups unrelated work. Did you mark warmup vs runtime?

omar: Also check if the kernel name is a JIT compile or a fallback kernel. In our last regression the kernel name had a "_ref" suffix indicating a fallback path.

matt: FYI OSRT sampling can be misleading at coarse intervals. We usually crank OSRT sampling and increase duration, or do a short full-trace bracket for the warmup section.

rebecca: Minimal repro options I rely on:
rebecca: ```
nsys profile \n  --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt,cudnn \n  --output=kv-warmup-dbg \n  --sample=osrt:interval=10us,cpu \n  --duration=20000 \n  --capture-range=nvtx:warmup\n```

rebecca: Use `nvtxRangePushA("warmup")`/`nvtxRangePop()` around the warmup path. Capture that bracket only and do a shorter full trace (no sampling) if you need exact timings.

alex: Good pointer. Is the osrt interval syntax exactly `osrt:interval=10us`? I remember versions differ.

omar: It varies by nsys release. Some versions accept `--sample=cpu,osrt:interval=10000` (value in ns) and newer allow `10us`. Check `nsys --version` and `nsys profile --help`.

julia: When you analyze: open the timeline, enable Samples lane, then enable Kernel lane names and filter by the suspicious blob time window. Look for repeated samples that align to multiple short kernels vs one long kernel. Sampling tends to show a long-looking box if there are many contiguous samples from different events.

matt: Another trick: export the callstack/sample table and sort by sample count for that kernel name. If total samples are low but avg duration reported high, it's probably sampling noise.

rebecca: For KV behaviour, compare token-level op logs with the trace. KV hits spawn lots of micros kernels (copy/evict) that sampling sometimes misses; the eviction/jit path can be a single heavy kernel and dominates samples.

alex: Plan: 1) add NVTX brackets around warmup 2) run long sampled capture (20s) with higher osrt sampling 3) if still ugly, do a short non-sampled full trace on only nvtx:warmup 4) paste the summary lines for the suspect kernel.

infra-bot: Reminder: reserve GPU profiling time on perf-lab: `@infra schedule perf-lab 1h` before ramping up captures.

omar: When iterating, include `--force-overwrite true` to avoid prompts in CI. Also consider a synthetic test that hits only the KV warmup path (single warm request) to reduce noise.

alex: Will run today and post the nsys summary lines (kernel name, total samples, avg duration, #calls). Thanks for the tips! :thumbsup:
